summary.text: 车 is the simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a wheeled vehicle. Its early forms show selected parts of a vehicle; the modern shape comes from cursive writing of 車.

formation.text: Pictographic: the traditional graph 車 depicts a vehicle through selected features, including wheels, body or frame, axle, yoke, pole, and crossbar. Early forms varied, and later writing reduced and regularized the picture. 車 is a whole-graph pictograph, so it has no separately analyzed components. The entry character 车 is a simplified graphic form of 車, not a separate pictographic construction.

components.text: The visible form 车 is the modern simplified character. Its source is the cursive form of 車, attested by the Sui dynasty at the latest; it was standardized in 1956. This is a graphic relationship, not a component analysis of the vehicle picture.

history.text: The traditional graph 車 appears in variable oracle-bone and bronze forms, with selected vehicle features represented; later forms reduced and regularized those depictions. The curated oracle-style, Western Zhou bronze-style, and seal-script images illustrate different presentations of the graph, but are modern redrawings rather than artifact photographs.

The modern simplified form 车 derives graphically from cursive 車. The dossier reports the cursive shape by the Sui dynasty at the latest and its adoption as a standard character in 1956; this standardization is distinct from the much earlier variation and simplification of traditional 車 forms.

uncertainties.text: The early vehicle depictions are supported by textual descriptions of variable forms; the supplied research did not visually inspect the glyph images, and particular details in any one drawing should be treated cautiously.

The dossier reports early inscription examples by corpus identifiers but gives no calendar dates for those individual inscriptions. It therefore does not establish a precise earliest date for the graph or its senses.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 車 for vehicles, and bronze examples include vehicles and war chariots. These reports establish early vehicle-related use, but not a calendar-dated first occurrence.
An oracle-bone example is reported as a place-name use. The evidence does not explain the name or connect it historically to the vehicle sense.

senses.gloss: wheeled machines; transporting by cart; cartload measure
senses.text: Dictionaries record these uses, but the supplied evidence does not date their emergence or establish a continuous development from the vehicle sense.
The common modern meaning includes vehicle and car.

limitations.text: The dossier does not establish the chronology or semantic links among the later machinery, transport, and measure senses, so they are recorded without a proposed chain of development.

Competing proposals connect the spoken word represented by 車 with Indo-Iranian wheel or chariot vocabulary. Such a proposal would mean a written sign for an older-sounding word was reused for a similar-sounding word, not that the pictured vehicle’s meaning developed into a new one. The source word for the depicted vehicle is not independently established here, and the proposed derivations remain disputed.
The traditional claim that Xi Zhong made the vehicle in the Xia period is transmitted historical tradition, not independently confirmed evidence in this dossier.

overview.text: 车 is a simplified way to write 車, whose early forms pictured a wheeled vehicle. The modern character’s shape comes from cursive writing of the traditional form.

components.text: This is the simplified character’s whole shape, derived from cursive 車; it is not a separate piece of the vehicle picture.

relationships.text: 车 is the modern simplified character derived from the cursive form of traditional 車.
